title: Child's marble-in-egg-carton: double-dot charge-position bit
idea: A child pictures a bit as 'which cup holds the marble', not 'how full is the cup'. Store ~50-200 electrons in one of two tunnel-coupled silicon quantum dots under a split gate: a write pulse tilts the double well, a raised inter-dot barrier holds the state, and a single-electron-transistor sensor reads which side is occupied without dumping charge onto a bitline.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and refresh (fact 3): total charge is conserved, so leakage to ground cannot erase the bit, only inter-dot tunneling can; ~100x less charge than a 5 fF cell and non-destructive read (fact 8).

title: 2D tunnel-diode bistable latch stacked in BEOL
idea: Shift the Goto-pair latch from III-V wafers to atomic layers: two WSe2/SnSe2 band-to-band tunnel diodes in series form a bistable node with negative differential resistance, plus one oxide access transistor, all in BEOL tiers.
why: 3D density: no capacitor, standby current in the pA range, stackable 10+ tiers over logic.

title: Twistor reborn: helical-anisotropy nanowires read by Wiedemann torsion pulses
idea: Bell's twistor wound magnetic tape helically on a copper wire. Electroplate vertical Cu-core/CoFe-shell nanowires under applied torsion so the shell has a helical easy axis, write helical domain segments by coincident axial current plus a tier strap, and read by the Wiedemann effect: a core current pulse twists each domain, launching a torsional acoustic echo sensed by an AlN piezo pad at the wire top.
why: A vertical wire is a 3D string with no transistor per tier (Fact 2); a mechanical readout signal sidesteps resistance-variation tails; ~64 bits per 20-nm wire.

title: Charge-density-wave phase bits in 1T-TaS2 films on sapphire
idea: Invert 'storage needs atoms or spins to move' -> store the bit in collective electron order. 1T-TaS2 switches between insulating and metallic charge-density-wave states with ps-ns electrical pulses and holds each with hysteresis; wafer-scale CVD TaS2 on sapphire gives cells read by a ~10-100x resistance contrast.
why: Purely electronic reconfiguration promises unlimited endurance, sub-ns writes and tiny volumes; room-temperature bistability (strain/doping-engineered hysteresis near the 350 K transition) is speculative.

title: MOS varactor storage node with self-amplifying C-V nonlinearity
idea: Combine an RF varactor with the storage capacitor: build the node as an accumulation-mode MOS capacitor whose capacitance is high when charged to '1' and drops ~3x near '0', so the stored charge difference exceeds that of a linear capacitor of the same average size. The C-V nonlinearity acts as built-in gain at charge-share time.
why: Fact 1: ~1.5-2x sense signal per unit area, which relaxes AR or allows a lower array voltage (fact 10).

title: Self-boosting MOS varactor capacitor doubles read charge
idea: MAGNIFY the signal with a nonlinear capacitor: the storage capacitor is a MOS varactor whose inversion threshold sits between the '0' and '1' levels, so a stored '1' is in high-capacitance inversion and a '0' in low-capacitance depletion; a plate pulse at read delivers ~2-3x the bitline charge difference of a linear capacitor of equal area.
why: Smaller capacitor for the same sense margin (fact 1) in any mature foundry eDRAM; smaller CV2 swing.

title: Eliminate plasma in 3D cells: vapor-HCl lateral etch carves horizontal capacitors
idea: Eliminate plasma steps in a 3D DRAM stack: grow 30-60 Si/SiGe bilayers by hydrogen-carrier CVD, cut slits, then use highly selective vapor HCl at 600-700 C to remove SiGe sideways and open the horizontal capacitor cavities and channel spaces in one gas-only, plasma-free step before ALD dielectric and electrode.
why: Attacks fact 2 (a manufacturable 3D cell needs 26+ tiers) by replacing many helium-cooled, argon-diluted HAR plasma etches with a thermal chemical etch; risks are selectivity across 60 tiers and strain-induced bowing.

title: F: fluorinated ferroelectric-nematic liquid crystal fills each storage well
idea: Fill nanoscale wells with a fluorinated ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (DIO-type, polarization ~5 uC/cm2, coercive field ~1,000x below oxide ferroelectrics) so the bit is the polar director orientation switched at ~1 V; fluid order cannot fatigue like a crystal, and anchoring defects that randomize ~1% of wells are tolerated.
why: Non-volatile, low-voltage polar storage (fact 10) filled by inkjet instead of ALD; switching speed of liquid crystal confined in nanowells is the main physics risk.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina nanopores multiply capacitor area for embargoed fabs
idea: A fab cut off from EUV, tungsten and helium can still anodize aluminum: one mask defines array regions in a BEOL Al layer that anodizes into self-ordered 20-30 nm pores at >100:1 aspect ratio, which are ALD-coated with TiN/ZrO2/TiN to form massive storage capacitors above the transistors. Self-assembly replaces HAR plasma etch and EUV patterning.
why: >=10 fF per cell without HAR etch tools (facts 1, 4) using abundant Al (scarce-resource intensity, U.S. manufacturability); registering pores to cells is the risk.

title: High-temperature superconductor persistent-current loops at 77 K
idea: Combine REBCO high-temperature superconductor films with an LN2 memory rack: each bit is a micro-loop holding a clockwise or counterclockwise persistent supercurrent (one flux quantum), written by a Josephson-junction pulse and read by an adjacent SQUID. Persistent currents do not decay, so refresh energy is zero and write energy is ~1e-19 J.
why: Zero refresh and sub-aJ writes; REBCO junction reproducibility and micron-scale loops limit density.

title: Landau-stabilized negative-capacitance boost layer inside storage capacitor
idea: Put a thin ferroelectric layer in series with the ZrO2-based dielectric and match the capacitances so the ferroelectric sits in its hysteresis-free negative-dC/dV Landau region. The series capacitance is then C_eff = C_d*|C_fe|/(|C_fe| - C_d), 3-5x above the dielectric alone.
why: Delivers the effective 'k ~ 70' that fact 1 calls for without new high-k chemistry, cutting capacitor aspect ratio from ~70:1 to ~20:1 with large etch and deposition capital savings.

title: Graveyard harvest fund for dead storage-element IP and engineers
idea: Systematically acquire lapsed or abandoned storage-element patent families (Z-RAM, T-RAM/VLT, Unity CMOx, Spin Memory PSC, Qimonda trench) and rehire their device engineers. Run each through a 'name the killer, fix only the killer' gate with a 90-day test-chip budget.
why: Starts on a decade of sunk R&D at pennies on the dollar, cutting time to first silicon by an estimated 2-4 years (capital and time axis).

title: Eliminate vacuum-deposited ferroelectrics: solution-grown croconic-acid proton-transfer bits
idea: Eliminate inorganic, vacuum-deposited ferroelectrics: grow the room-temperature organic ferroelectric croconic acid (Ps ~20 uC/cm2) from solution inside cell pores, where polarization reverses by collective proton transfer along hydrogen bonds, a light-particle switch that needs small fields and no oxygen-vacancy motion.
why: Nonvolatile storage at low coercive voltage (fact 10) made by solution casting with no process gases; proton transfer avoids the vacancy-driven fatigue of HZO; risks are thermal budget, thin-film quality and BEOL integration.

title: Mood ring: fluorine-free ferroelectric nematic fluid in nanowells
idea: Stimulus 'mood ring' (liquid crystal that changes state) -> fill 20 nm wells with an RM734-class ferroelectric nematic liquid crystal (a polar fluid with ~6 uC/cm^2 and no fluorine, unlike most display LCs); a field pulse flips the polar director up or down and boundary anchoring holds it, read as a polarization current or capacitance. A fluid self-heals, so there are no fatigue-causing defects.
why: Fatigue-free polar storage with low switching voltage (fact 10) and no refresh (fact 3), filled by capillary action with no etch (fact 4).

title: Leaky floating gate with direct-tunneling oxide for unlimited writes
idea: MINIFY the tunnel oxide to ~2.5 nm so writes use direct tunneling at ~2 V in ~10 ns instead of damaging Fowler-Nordheim injection, accepting seconds-to-hours retention; a 10-person team runs it on a 180-nm university or MPW-compatible flow with a poly floating gate.
why: Quasi-volatile memory refreshed ~1000x less than DRAM (fact 3), capacitor-free (fact 1), endurance >1e12 because direct-tunnel stress is low; U.S. mature-node manufacturable.

title: Geologist's fault lines: conductive ferroelectric domain-wall bits in LiNbO3
idea: A geologist knows fluids flow along faults, not through solid rock. In thin-film single-crystal LiNbO3, writing a nanoscale reversed domain creates a charged domain wall that conducts ~1e4x better than the bulk; the bit is 'wall present or absent' and is read non-destructively as a current.
why: Non-destructive read (fact 8), non-volatile storage (fact 3), and ferroelectric switching endurance above 1e10 with no high-AR capacitor (fact 1).

title: Fairchild CCD memory reborn as vertical IGZO buried-channel CCD
idea: 1970s CCD memories died from serial access and silicon dark current that filled potential wells within ms when hot. Stack 64-128 gate tiers 3D-NAND-style around a vertical IGZO channel, store electron packets under alternate gates and shift a few stages to a top sense node. IGZO has no holes to invert the channel and a ~3.1 eV gap, so thermal generation stays negligible at 125 C and packets last seconds or more.
why: 3D DRAM with no capacitor and no per-tier transistor (Fact 2), ~10x bits per litho layer; retention far beyond 64 ms even at 125 C.

title: Swap destructive charge dump for small-signal capacitive ferroelectric read
idea: Build asymmetric-electrode ferroelectric capacitors (for example TiN/HZO/W-oxide) whose small-signal capacitance differs by 20-40% between the two polarization states. A ~100 mV AC probe senses that capacitance without switching the cell, and the films stack in 3D by deposition at DUV pitch.
why: No destructive read and no write-back (fact 8), and no refresh (fact 3). Writes are rare, so ferroelectric endurance limits matter less, and 3D stacking by deposition needs no EUV (facts 2, 4).

title: MOS-varactor storage node read nondestructively by RF capacitance sensing
idea: KV caches read each bit thousands of times, so one added implant mask converts the storage node into a depletion-type MOS varactor whose capacitance depends on its stored voltage; a small high-frequency probe on the plate senses that capacitance via the bitline without draining charge. Writes stay conventional; reads stop being destructive.
why: Kills destructive read and restore energy (fact 8, ~5.9 pJ per useful bit) and the activations that drive row hammer (fact 9); detecting small capacitance changes on long bitlines is the risk.

title: Thin-film magnetic core memory with zero transistors in the array
idea: Invert 'modern memory must be built from semiconductor transistors' -> revive coincident-current magnetic cores in thin film. Sub-micron permalloy rings electroplated around crossing X/Y/sense lines on glass or ceramic switch only when two half-currents coincide, storing the bit as flux direction with nanosecond thin-film switching and no transistor per cell.
why: Unlimited endurance, non-volatile, radiation-hard, uses only Ni, Fe and Cu (no tungsten, EUV or silicon wafer); ~1 um^2 cells make it a niche or capacity tier, and destructive read plus half-select margins are the risks.

title: Electrophoretic nanoparticle bit shuttling across a printed nanocell
idea: IFR: e-paper bistability at DRAM speed. Closest achievable: confine one charged nanoparticle in a printed ~10 nm fluid cell; a field pulse drives it to either electrode (transit ~10 ns at 10 nm), van der Waals force holds it there, and the bit reads as a capacitance shift.
why: Zero retention power, no solid-state wear (unlimited endurance), printable fluid cells.

title: Fe: iron-triazole spin-crossover nanoparticles store bits as spin state
idea: Fill each cell with a few 10 nm [Fe(Htrz)2(trz)] spin-crossover particles whose low-spin and high-spin states coexist inside a thermal hysteresis loop near chip temperature; a current pulse flips the spin state, changing conductance ~10x, and particle spread causing ~1% misreads is absorbed by majority voting across three cells.
why: Molecule-scale non-volatile storage from Fe, C, N and H synthesized in a flask, with no high-AR etch (facts 1, 4); switching speed and cyclability are the open questions.

title: Redox-molecule monolayer: quantized one-electron-per-molecule pseudocapacitive storage
idea: Line a shallow 20 nm x 200 nm hole (10:1 AR) with a room-temperature self-assembled monolayer of ferrocene/porphyrin redox molecules on short conjugated linkers (~1e14 per cm2), with a solid polymer electrolyte supplying counter-ions. Each molecule stores exactly one electron at a fixed Nernstian potential, ~12,000 e per cell, sensed as a potential step.
why: Faradaic charge per area beats dielectric charge, so a 10:1 well matches a 70:1 pillar (fact 1). Electron transfer must reach >1e8 per second.

title: Tunnel-FET access device eliminates the thermionic leakage tail
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): same timings, so the write must still finish within tWR. Replace the access MOSFET with a vertical SiGe/Si tunnel FET whose off state relies on band misalignment rather than a thermionic barrier, so subthreshold leakage drops below 0.01 fA and barely changes with temperature, while its lower on-current still charges 5 fF within tWR.
why: Removes the leakage tail (fact 3) and the 2x hot-temperature refresh penalty, reported via the existing refresh-rate register; on-current and ambipolar leakage are the risks.

title: Swap gate-dielectric polarization for ferroelectric semiconductor channel (alpha-In2Se3)
idea: Use a 2D ferroelectric semiconductor such as alpha-In2Se3, where the polarization lives inside the channel itself. Flipping it shifts the band bending and so the channel conductance, with no ferroelectric/dielectric interface to trap charge or depolarize.
why: Gives a capacitor-less 1T cell with non-destructive read and no refresh (facts 1, 3, 8), and avoids the endurance loss that limits HZO FeFETs.

title: Coin-counting purse: single-electron box stores countable electron numbers
idea: Count coins instead of weighing gold: couple a 3-5-nm Si or Pt island (e-beam litho plus oxidation thinning, or ALD nanoparticle) through one tunnel junction to a reservoir so Coulomb blockade (>150 meV charging energy) makes occupancy discrete; each cell stores 0-3 extra electrons (2 bits), read by a nearby single-electron transistor electrometer without disturbing the count.
why: Fact 10 and energy: writes of a few electrons at ~0.2 V are attojoule-scale and multi-level states are quantized rather than analog; RT operation needs sub-5-nm islands, and random background-charge offsets are the classic killer.

title: Po: memory is baked like pottery — co-fired ceramic ferroelectric crossbar
idea: Po: memory is baked like pottery. Extracted: use MLCC tape casting to stack ~1,000 sub-um BaTiO3 layers with printed Ni electrodes running X and Y on alternate layers; each crossing is a ferroelectric capacitor bit and the coercive field acts as the selector (V/3 half-select), so the block contains no transistors.
why: MLCC lines make 1,000-layer blocks for fractions of a cent: ~1e8 crossings/cm2/layer x 1,000 layers is ~12 GB per cm2 footprint for cents, well over 100x cheaper per GB. Trade-offs: us latency, destructive read, edge-wiring thousands of lines to a CMOS driver die.

title: Eliminate the leakage tail in place: on-die electrothermal annealing of weak cells
idea: Eliminate retention-weak tail cells without furnaces or forming-gas and argon anneals: drive a short high current through selected wordline segments so Joule heating takes the local access transistors to ~300-400 C for microseconds, annealing the interface and junction traps behind variable-retention-time and GIDL tail cells; the controller targets the cells its retention profiler flags.
why: Shrinks the <=13 fA leakage tail (fact 3) so the refresh interval can stretch 4-8x, using no process gases at all; risks are thermal disturb of neighbors and wordline electromigration.

title: Proton-doped nickelate bit: electron filling flips resistance a millionfold
idea: Effect walk: ion migration driving a Mott transition. A 10-nm SmNiO3 channel exchanges H+ with an adjacent nanometre proton reservoir; each inserted proton donates an electron that localizes on Ni (Ni3+ to Ni2+), turning the metal into a strongly correlated insulator with up to ~10^6 resistance change, read at ~50 mV.
why: Holds state without refresh (fact 3) and the enormous read margin removes full sense-amp restore (fact 8); a vertical 4F2 BEOL stack with no capacitor; proton endurance (>10^12 cycles needed) and ns kinetics are the open risks.

title: Po: memory spins — MEMS magnetic micro-carousel with fixed head arrays
idea: Po: memory spins. Extracted: a mm-scale MEMS rotor coated with perpendicular magnetic media spins at ~100k rpm under 1,000 stationary on-chip MTJ read/write heads, so each head serves one narrow track and the average wait is ~0.3 ms.
why: Brings HDD-class media cost (~$0.015/GB, ~500x below DRAM) to chip scale as a warm tier behind a small DRAM. Trade-offs: ms latency and mechanical wear.

title: Deep-trench storage caps from US trench-power MOSFET fabs
idea: Worsen: claim only DRAM fabs can etch high-AR capacitors. Flip: trench-MOSFET power fabs (mature 200 mm, US-based) already etch deep silicon trenches daily; fund ~$700k of engineering lots to make 40:1 trench capacitors at 200 nm pitch as the storage layer of a 3D-bonded memory die.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: depreciated 200 mm tools, and IBM eDRAM already proved trench storage caps.

title: Error-tolerant AI cells with half-height capacitors and BER budget
idea: LLM weights and activations survive ~1e-5 bit error rates in low-order mantissa bits, so an 'approximate' DRAM grade uses 2-2.5 fF capacitors at AR ~30:1 with longer refresh, while sign and exponent bits live in a few full-charge rows of the same mat. The storage element is deliberately under-built where the extreme user does not care.
why: Halves capacitor aspect ratio (fact 1), cutting HAR etch/deposition cost and refresh power ~2x for the ~70% of AI bits that tolerate noise: roughly 15-25% cost-per-bit gain.

title: HPE memristor's wandering vacancies ordered: brownmillerite-perovskite topotactic switching
idea: TiO2 memristors failed hot because disordered oxygen vacancies diffused and filaments relaxed. Use an SrFeO2.5 brownmillerite film whose vacancies sit in ordered channels: a field converts a nanoscale region topotactically to conductive perovskite SrFeO3-d, so the two states are distinct crystal phases separated by a structural barrier rather than a diffusing cloud.
why: Phase-distinct states give 125 C/10 y retention with area-type, non-filament switching and low variability.

title: Spin-crossover molecular films switching high and low spin states
idea: Invert 'the bit is a charge, polarization or magnetic direction' -> store it as a molecule's spin state. Room-temperature-hysteretic Fe(II) spin-crossover complexes vacuum-sublimed onto glass or polymer flip between low and high spin (with ~10% volume and large conductance change) under a gate-induced charge or strain pulse inside their hysteresis loop, read by tunneling current.
why: Non-volatile inside the hysteresis window, ~2 nm molecular cells, no scarce elements and low-temperature processing on any substrate; field-driven switching speed and room-temperature margins are speculative.

title: Ti: adhesion-latched TiN nanorelay holds bit by van der Waals
idea: A 10 nm TiN cantilever is pulled into contact with the storage pad and held by surface adhesion with no power, then released by a reverse-polarity pull-off pulse; the ~1% of cells that stay stuck or fail to latch per scrub interval are treated as erasures by the code.
why: Zero-leakage, refresh-free bit (fact 3) from CMOS-standard TiN, where stiction, the classic NEMS killer, is used as the latch and its failures are budgeted instead of engineered out.

title: Pseudocapacitive redox storage node borrowed from supercapacitors
idea: Coat the storage-node electrode with 1-2 nm of hydrous MnO2 (or another fast surface-redox oxide) behind a thin blocking oxide, so surface faradaic reactions store charge on top of the dielectric's electrostatic charge, as in supercapacitor electrodes (hundreds of uF/cm2). The cell becomes a nano-supercapacitor with 10-50x the areal charge of a plain MIM stack.
why: Fact 1: a planar or AR<10 capacitor could reach 5 fF, collapsing the high-AR etch and multi-step ALD module (cost per bit, capital); the open question is whether redox kinetics keep up at ns timescales.

title: Core memory reborn: electroplated permalloy nano-toroid stacks
idea: Swap charge for flux: plate 1 um permalloy rings around through-mask copper posts (1990s thin-film-head plating) in 20 tiers, select by coincident X/Y half-currents and sense on a shared winding, a destructive read like DRAM but with zero leakage and unlimited endurance.
why: Refresh and standby power (fact 3), U.S. manufacturability via disk-head plating know-how; ~0.05 um2/bit across 20 tiers (still ~60x DRAM area), aimed at refresh-free persistent buffers.

title: HBM-pin-compatible core dies built in U.S. logic fabs with deep-trench cells
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): drop into existing HBM3E stacks and controllers. Fabricate core dies in U.S. logic foundries on their deep-trench eDRAM process (bulk-Si trench caps of ~30-40 fF), stack them on a standard HBM base die, and sell them as lower-density but available HBM for inference tiers.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital (fact 4; U.S. makes 1-2% of DRAM): reuses depreciated logic capacity with no new DRAM fab; ~1/3 DRAM density but viable at 4x prices.

title: Solar-cell black silicon: litho-free nanograss electrodes multiply capacitor area
idea: Solar cells use maskless cryogenic SF6/O2 RIE to grow self-masked 'black silicon' needles 1-2 um tall at ~100-nm spacing; apply the same etch to texture each capacitor's bottom electrode for a 10-20x area gain, then line it conformally by ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN so each cell pad needs only coarse contact lithography.
why: Facts 1 and 4: 10-20x capacitance per footprint without EUV or a patterned high-AR etch, using one ICP-RIE plus ALD; Poisson variation in needle count sets a ~100-nm minimum pad, so it fits relaxed-pitch U.S. commodity or gain-cell storage.

title: Si: 20:1 pillars at 1.5 fF accept 1% sense misses
idea: Cut the silicon-supported capacitor to 20:1 (~1.5 fF) and run the sense amp at ~2.3 sigma margin, which misreads ~1% of cells, then protect each 512-bit burst with an on-die LDPC code of ~12% overhead that brings output BER below 1e-15.
why: Removes about two thirds of the capacitor etch/deposit height and lets the pitch shrink (facts 1, 4); net cost per bit falls an estimated 20-30% even after ECC overhead.

title: Datacenter fiber loops store bits as light in flight
idea: Jump to datacenter scale and to time of flight: coil 10-50 km of fiber per rack and circulate WDM pulse trains with amplification; a 20 km loop at 64 channels x 100 Gb/s holds about 0.6 Gb in transit for streaming tensors.
why: Scarce resources: memory capacity from mature telecom fiber and lasers, with no DRAM wafers, for sequential-access buffers.

title: Po: memory you read by listening — piezo-sensed AlScN ferroelectric bit
idea: Po: memory you read by listening to it. Extracted: store the bit in wurtzite AlScN polarization and read it non-destructively with a small sub-coercive AC drive; the sign of the piezoelectric response (charge or acoustic phase) reveals the polarization without ever switching it.
why: Non-destructive ferroelectric read removes restore energy and read-induced fatigue (fact 8). Nanoscale signal size is the risk.

title: Lithium-niobate domain-wall conduction bit on purchased LNOI wafers
idea: MINIFY the readout to a domain wall: on commercial thin-film lithium-niobate-on-insulator, a ~1-2 V pulse between surface electrodes nucleates a nanoscale inverted domain whose charged walls conduct ~nA; read non-destructively at sub-coercive voltage, erased by reverse pulse. Needs only a stepper, metal lift-off and an etcher.
why: Non-destructive read (fact 8), nonvolatile so no refresh (fact 3), LN wall cells have shown >1e10 cycles; minimal tooling.

title: Imprint as a feature: work-function-biased antiferroelectric bistable cell
idea: Reverse a reliability defect into the design: asymmetric electrodes (~1 eV work-function gap) or a fixed dipole layer around antiferroelectric ZrO2 shift one of its double-hysteresis loops to straddle 0 V, making the AFE bistable at zero bias while keeping AFE's high endurance (no FE domain pinning, target >1e15 cycles).
why: Refresh and voltage floor (facts 3,10): nonvolatile zero-bias storage written at ~1 V by a field-induced transition, removing refresh energy.

title: Swiss banker's safe-deposit boxes: polyoxometalate multi-electron cell
idea: A banker keeps many items in one vault. Polyoxometalate clusters (e.g., [PW12O40]3-) accept 2-6 extra electrons in discrete, well-separated redox steps. A grafted monolayer of them forms the storage node and holds 2-3 bits per cell, read as distinct voltage plateaus.
why: 2-3 bits per cell multiplies density 2-3x at the same lithography (fact 4); discrete redox levels give better noise margins than analog multi-level charge.

title: Photodiode storage node written by co-packaged laser light
idea: Laser-crosslink satellites receive data as light, so one implant mask turns storage nodes into Si photodiode junctions under a transparent plate; rows are precharged to '1' and a modulated micro-LED/VCSEL array discharges the '0' cells optically in parallel, while reads stay electrical. Write drivers and write bitline swings largely disappear.
why: Cuts write data-movement energy (fact 5) and periphery (fact 7) for streaming-write workloads; optical alignment and neighbor crosstalk are the risks.

title: Hot-zone beachhead: launch where silicon DRAM hurts most
idea: Nantero, Optane and early MRAM died without a market where they beat DRAM on day one. Launch a 125 C-native storage element first in Grade-1 automotive and industrial LPDDR sockets, where silicon DRAM must refresh ~8x faster and derate, and pre-sell to Tier-1s with 10-year supply contracts that fund the fab ramp.
why: Turns the constraint into a price premium (~1.5-3x $/bit tolerated), funds capital intensity from early revenue and builds U.S. volume.

title: Polar-vortex superlattice dielectric with stabilized negative capacitance
idea: MAGNIFY effective permittivity ~10x by building the cell dielectric from 1-2 nm alternating lead-free BaTiO3/SrTiO3 layers whose polar vortices contribute a stabilized negative capacitance; the series stack nets k ~250-400 without hysteresis because the vortex state never fully switches.
why: Clears the k~70 requirement (fact 1) with margin, so capacitor AR could fall from ~70:1 to ~15:1, cutting etch steps and freeing height budget for tiers.

title: Liquid-nitrogen DRAM: freeze out leakage, then shrink the capacitor
idea: Run the array at 77 K, where thermally activated leakage (junction generation, subthreshold, trap-assisted) falls by >1e6 because it scales as exp(-Ea/kT). Design out the weakly temperature-dependent GIDL with a lower wordline-off bias, so a 0.3 fF planar MIM holds data for hours and refresh is dropped. Racks are LN2-cooled at ~10x wall-power overhead on the much smaller memory heat.
why: Removes refresh (fact 3) and the capacitor charge wall (fact 1). Planar caps can approach 4F2 with no pillar etch, and bitline resistance falls ~5x.

title: Gecko peel-angle latch: adhesive nanoflap released by torque, not force
idea: Gecko setae grip by van der Waals force but release at once when peeled at ~30 degrees. Make the bit a hinged graphene or SiN nanoflap that sticks flat to either face of a V-shaped trench. A small electrode at the hinge applies peeling torque, so release needs ~10x less voltage than a straight pull-off, while adhesion holds the state with no power.
why: Non-volatile mechanical bit written at ~1 V instead of the 5-10 V of NEMS contact switches, which helps with the voltage floor (fact 10) and with stiction failure. Read by capacitance.

title: Bacteria-grown magnetite nanocrystals as self-made single-domain bits
idea: Invert 'storage elements are fabricated in a fab' -> grow them. Magnetotactic bacteria biomineralize near-perfect 40-50 nm single-domain magnetite crystals at room temperature from iron salts; purified magnetosomes are placed by DNA-origami or field-guided assembly onto glass carrying spin-orbit-torque write lines and Hall read contacts.
why: Ultra-uniform nanomagnets with zero vacuum or litho capex for the storage element, abundant iron (scarce-resource intensity), non-volatile with unlimited endurance; placement precision and switching current are speculative.

title: Phase-state NEMS parametron for megagray nuclear reactor instrumentation
idea: Reactor instruments absorb megagray doses that wreck oxides and stored charge, so bits are stored as the oscillation phase (0 or pi) of parametrically pumped nanobeams, as in 1950s parametron computers; one release mask lets a vapor etch free beams from an existing BEOL metal layer. A shared pump keeps beams oscillating and reads detect phase capacitively.
why: Radiation-immune, refresh-free while pumped and wear-free; low density (~um2/bit) makes it a niche tier, but it proves charge-free storage in BEOL for one mask.

title: Porphyrin redox monolayer adds quantized charge states to every capacitor
idea: TRIZ #5 Merging: graft a self-assembled monolayer of multi-state redox molecules (porphyrin/ferrocene dyads) onto the storage electrode so each molecule adds 1-2 electrons at fixed oxidation potentials. Charge density reaches ~10-30 uC/cm2 versus ~5 for high-k at 1 V, and the discrete potentials give native 2-bit cells.
why: Fact 1: 3-5x Cs per area; fact 10: multi-level storage at fixed, low voltages.

title: Chlorophyll special-pair redox monolayer as the storage node
idea: Photosynthetic reaction centres store charge as molecular oxidation states. Coat the node electrode with a self-assembled porphyrin or chlorophyll-analog monolayer under a thin solid polymer electrolyte. Each molecule stores 1-2 electrons at discrete potentials, giving pseudocapacitance of ~50-100 uC/cm2, about 10x a high-k MIM, so a low-AR cell holds a full signal.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): ~10x charge per area could take AR from 70 to below 10 and remove the deep etch. Discrete redox potentials also allow multilevel cells.

title: Hard-disk TDMR detection lets storage nodes crowd and crosstalk
idea: Adapt two-dimensional magnetic recording: shrink node pitch until neighbors couple ~25% (no isolation spacers), read each row together with its two neighbors, and decode jointly with a 2D Viterbi/MAP equalizer in the sense-amp stripe, at 2 levels per node.
why: 10x at same cost: ~2.5x from pitch, 2x from levels, 2x from a second deposited tier; no new litho node, because crosstalk is cancelled rather than prevented.

title: Noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn tunnel junction with zero stray field
idea: Box = {medium: magnetic octupole order in Mn3Sn | access: Si FinFET | sense: antiferromagnetic tunnel magnetoresistance | integration: BEOL above periphery | substrate: Si | fab: sputtered Mn3Sn on a Pt spin-orbit-torque line, 400 C anneal}. Spin-orbit torque rotates the octupole; with no net magnetization, cells at 15 nm pitch do not disturb neighbors and switch in tens of picoseconds.
why: Density and energy: removes the stray-field pitch limit of ferromagnetic MRAM, sub-100 ps writes at ~10 fJ, built from abundant Mn and Sn.

title: Mixed-conductor volumetric capacitance storage node from wearable bioelectronics
idea: Wearable sensors use organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors such as PEDOT:PSS whose entire volume charges at ~40 F/cm3, so a 100 nm cube stores ~40 fF, ~8x a DRAM pillar. A sealed solid-electrolyte version (polymerized ionic liquid) aims for 10-100 ns charging because ion diffusion time shrinks with the square of size.
why: Destroys the capacitor charge wall (fact 1) with no high aspect ratio and leaves room for multi-level storage; ion speed and 1e15-cycle stability are unproven.

title: Non-collinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn bit with zero stray field
idea: TRIZ #13 Other way round: instead of a ferromagnet (MRAM, already examined), store the bit in the octupole order of a non-collinear antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn) switched by spin-orbit torque from an underlying heavy-metal or topological line and read by its large anomalous Hall or tunnel magnetoresistance. Zero net moment means no stray-field coupling and ~10-ps switching.
why: Facts 3 and 9: nonvolatile with no refresh, immune to row-hammer-style neighbor coupling, and packable at 2-3F2 because there are no stray fields.

title: Venus flytrap snap-buckling nanobeam with coincidence-only write
idea: The flytrap leaf is a prestressed shell that snaps between two curvatures. Make each bit a pre-compressed buckled nanobeam (200 nm SiC or AlScN) resting up or down, read by capacitance to a sense electrode. Snap-through needs the row and column electrodes energized together, because either half-voltage alone only bends the beam elastically, which gives crosspoint selection with no transistor.
why: Non-volatile, with no access transistor, no leakage and no refresh. SiC beams at low strain have fatigue limits beyond 10^12 cycles, and MEMS fabs are US-based.

title: Storage-element prize judged on a common 300 mm test vehicle
idea: IFR: the perfect bit shows up because everyone tries. Closest achievable: a $50M tiered prize (<=4F^2, >=1 s retention, <=10 ns, >=1e15 cycles) where finalists integrate their storage element on a shared U.S. 300 mm wafer that already carries real sense amps and periphery.
why: Speeds storage-element discovery and U.S. manufacturability; the shared periphery wafer cuts each team's capital need ~100x.

title: Liquid-metal droplet position bit in printed microchannels
idea: IFR: a bit held by surface tension at zero power. Closest achievable: a sub-um gallium-alloy droplet rests in one of two pinned pockets of a printed channel; an electrocapillary pulse moves it and the bit is read as the capacitance of the occupied pocket.
why: Unlimited endurance (no solid wear), zero retention power, printable; latency scales with size and is the main risk.

title: O: topotactic oxygen shuttle toggles CaFeO2.5 insulator and CaFeO3 metal
idea: Place a ~5 nm brownmillerite CaFeO2.5 layer against an oxygen-reservoir oxide; a field pulse fills or empties its pre-ordered vacancy channels so the whole film converts topotactically to metallic perovskite CaFeO3 and back, read as a 10-100x resistance change.
why: Uniform phase conversion through ordered channels avoids the random filaments of ReRAM, removing forming and most variability; all Ca/Fe/O; ns switching and endurance are unproven.

title: Printed proton-transfer organic ferroelectric with low coercive voltage
idea: IFR: polarization that flips without moving heavy atoms. Closest achievable: solution-print croconic acid or diisopropylammonium bromide films whose polarization reverses by proton hopping along hydrogen bonds (P ~20 uC/cm^2) at low field, used as printed capacitors in a 2T nondestructive-read gain configuration.
why: Fact 10 and capital: organic ferroelectric printed below 150 C with remanent polarization comparable to HZO.

title: MLCC-style tape-cast 3D capacitor stack for printed DRAM
idea: IFR: 3D DRAM capacitors made the way industry already prints trillions of MLCCs a year. Closest achievable: tape-cast and screen-print 0.5 um BaTiO3 layers (k~2000) with printed Ni electrodes into a 100-layer stack whose per-layer pads are addressed by printed oxide-TFT selectors on the stack edge; 1 um^2 at 0.5 um already gives ~35 fF.
why: Facts 1 and 2: 7x the needed charge without high AR; MLCC lines use no EUV and cost cents per part, so capital per bit drops by orders.

title: Dealloyed nanoporous metal sponge multiplies capacitor surface tenfold
idea: MAGNIFY electrode area: deposit a Ru-Al or Ti-Al alloy liner in a shallow capacitor hole, selectively leach the Al to leave a metal sponge with 3-5 nm pores, then coat with ALD ZrO2 and a plate electrode, giving ~10x the internal surface of a smooth cylinder.
why: Same ~5 fF at AR ~10:1 instead of 70:1 (fact 1), removing the hardest etch and making capacitors stackable; conformal dielectric inside the pores is the risk.

title: Buried-oxide-isolated storage nodes immune to row hammer coupling
idea: Forced limit (DDR/HBM interface unchanged): controllers keep sending the same RFM and refresh, so the cell itself must stop flipping. Isolate each storage-node junction from the shared substrate with a local buried-oxide pocket (selective SiGe removal and oxidation) and shield it with a grounded buried plate between adjacent wordlines, cutting the electron-injection and trap-assisted paths that aggressor activations exploit.
why: Raises the row-hammer threshold from ~1k to >100k activations (fact 9), removing mitigation overhead, and trims the junction-leakage tail (fact 3).

title: NEMS air-gap relay as zero-leakage access switch for capacitor
idea: Replace the access transistor with a vertical nanoelectromechanical relay whose off state is a 5 nm vacuum gap: no channel and no junction, so off-current is essentially zero and the capacitor keeps its charge for days, limited only by dielectric leakage. Carbon or TiN contacts sit under a hermetic BEOL cap, and a negative-stiffness spring lets the relay close in a few ns below 1 V.
why: Fact 3: the 13 fA leakage tail vanishes, so refresh drops from ~46 fJ/bit to zero; low pull-in voltage also removes the 3 V wordline (fact 10).

title: Bamboo forest: grow capacitor pillars upward instead of etching them
idea: Stimulus 'bamboo forest' (tall shoots grow up, nobody carves them) -> pattern a thin Al2O3 mask with BCl3/Cl2, then grow vertical Si/SiGe nanopillars by selective-area epitaxy (SiH4/HCl) to 100:1 and convert them into bottom electrodes with chloride-ALD TiN. Height comes from growth time, not a deep fluorocarbon etch.
why: Decouples pillar aspect ratio from etch physics (fact 1) and drops the hardest etch/EUV layer (fact 4); fluorine-free end to end.

title: Pulsed-power antiferroelectric charge release triples DRAM read signal
idea: Pulsed-power capacitors use antiferroelectrics because field-induced polarization dumps large charge on discharge; a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric capacitor written to '1' sits in the field-induced polar state and, during charge sharing, back-switches to release ~3-5x the charge of a linear dielectric, while a '0' releases only linear charge. No remanence is used, so fatigue stays modest.
why: Effective k ~100+ during read (fact 1) lets the pillar drop from 70:1 to ~25:1; the '1' level must exceed the ~1.5 MV/cm forward switching field, partly fighting the voltage floor (fact 10).

title: C: pre-buckled amorphous-carbon nanobeam snaps between two stable shapes
idea: Deposit a 5 nm x 80 nm a-C:H (diamond-like carbon) bridge under built-in compressive stress so it buckles up or down; an electrostatic pulse from an under- or over-electrode snaps it across (GHz-class resonance gives ~1 ns transit) and the gap capacitance or tunneling current reads it.
why: Elastic bistability holds the bit with zero leakage: no refresh (fact 3), no charge wall (fact 1), carbon from methane PECVD; stiction and fatigue over 1e15 cycles are the risks.

title: Matryoshka doll: lithium ion rattling inside a fullerene cage
idea: Stimulus 'nesting doll' -> Li+@C60 endohedral fullerenes, where the ion sits off-centre in one of several wells inside the cage; a monolayer sits on a FET gate and a field pulse pushes each ion to the 'top' or 'bottom' well, whose dipole shifts the FET threshold. The cage shields the ion from chemistry and moisture.
why: Single-molecule bit (~1 nm^2) with no capacitor (fact 1) and threshold readout that does not destroy the state (fact 8); potential 100x density if room-temperature wells are deep enough.

title: Dekatron glow-stepping counter revived as a multi-position domain-wall cell
idea: The Dekatron stored a decimal digit as the position of one glow among ten cathodes. Store 4 bits as the position of a single domain wall among 16 notches in a 400-nm magnetic strip, stepped by current pulses and read by an MTJ whose free layer overlaps a wedge so resistance tracks wall position.
why: 4 bits per cell instead of 1 gives density without a litho shrink (Fact 4), non-volatile with no capacitor (Facts 1, 3); risk is separating 16 resistance levels.

title: Swap dielectric charge for porphyrin redox monolayer storing discrete electrons
idea: Graft a tripodal porphyrin or ferrocene self-assembled monolayer onto the storage electrode, with a solid electrolyte. The bit is held as molecular oxidation states (two states give 1.5 bits per cell) at ~10^14 molecules/cm2, or about 16-30 uC/cm2 per state; ZettaCore showed 400 C survivability and 10^12 cycles.
why: 3-4x charge per area over a linear cap (fact 1), so a 15:1 cap at DUV pitch works, and retention of minutes cuts refresh ~1000x (fact 3); the monolayer self-assembles with no lithography.

title: Swap charge for molecular spin state in spin-crossover nanocrystals
idea: Store the bit as the low-spin or high-spin state of Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover nanocrystals, which are bistable inside a thermal hysteresis loop centred on the die's operating temperature. A field or current pulse switches the state, and the read senses the ~10^2 change in conductance or permittivity.
why: Non-volatile, so no refresh (fact 3). The solution chemistry is cheap, uses abundant Fe and N with no chokepoint elements, and makes a 2-terminal crossbar that stacks.

title: Rescue reject-bin DRAM die by remapping only the weak cells
idea: Worsen: scrap dies because a few thousand storage cells leak too fast. Flip: buy fail-bin and downgraded dies cheaply, run a 24-month retention census on an FPGA tester to map weak cells, and ship modules whose controller remaps those cells or refreshes them more often.
why: Raises usable supply now; salvaged dies cost ~30-50% of new per bit, and the program needs ~$1M of capital.

title: Vertical CCD strings on 3D-NAND tooling as capacitorless 3D DRAM
idea: Invert 'every bit needs its own capacitor and access transistor at a fixed site' -> bits are charge packets that march. A vertical oxide-semiconductor or epitaxial channel threads 64-128 word-plane tiers clocked as a 3-phase CCD, so each pillar holds dozens of packets shifted to one sense/regenerate node at its top.
why: A 3D DRAM with no capacitor and no lateral transistor (fact 2) built in depreciated 3D-NAND fabs; area per bit ~pillar pitch^2/tiers gives >5x DDR5 density, refresh happens automatically every lap; latency ~tiers x shift time (~30-60 ns).

title: All-silicon vertical gated thyristor: bistable bit from boron, phosphorus, silicon
idea: Box = {medium: regenerative pnpn latch state | access: the thyristor's own gate | sense: on/off current ~1e5 | integration: vertical 4F2 pillars | substrate: U.S. Si | fab: in-situ doped epitaxy with California boron and U.S. phosphate phosphorus, NiSi contacts from Michigan nickel}. The cell contains only Si, B, P, O, N and Ni, so it needs no capacitor dielectric and no exotic metal.
why: U.S. manufacturability and scarce resources: a 4F2 cell that needs little refresh, with the shortest supply chain possible.

title: Negative-capacitance ferroelectric layer boosts storage capacitance for 0.5-V hearing aids
idea: Hearing aids run from ~1 V cells and want sub-0.5 V arrays; a stabilized negative-capacitance HZO layer in series with a ZrO2 positive capacitor makes the stack's effective capacitance exceed either layer alone, behaving like k~100-200. The extra charge keeps the same sense signal at half the array voltage.
why: Attacks the charge wall (fact 1) and CV2 voltage floor (fact 10): ~2-4x lower energy per bit if NC stays hysteresis-free at ns speed, a contested claim.

title: Antiferroelectric ZrO2 phase switch pumps extra charge
idea: Scale down to the lattice: operate the capacitor dielectric as an antiferroelectric whose field-induced tetragonal-to-orthorhombic transition releases a burst of polarization charge above a threshold voltage, then fully returns at zero field (no remanence, no wake-up fatigue).
why: Capacitor wall: 2-3x charge per pillar at the same AR; nonlinear charge also sharpens sense margin.

title: Ramtron's capacitor repurposed: antiferroelectric charge-dump DRAM storage node
idea: Ferroelectric capacitors failed in FeRAM because reads were destructive and fatigue accumulated, but DRAM reads are destructive anyway. Use a ZrO2-rich antiferroelectric whose field-induced polar phase stores ~15-25 uC/cm2 of extra charge above its switching field and back-switches on read, dumping that charge onto the bitline.
why: 2-4x effective charge per capacitor area at the same height, cutting the needed aspect ratio from ~115 toward ~40 (Fact 1); uses existing ZrO2 ALD tools.

title: Mitochondrial cristae lamellar capacitor for lateral 3D DRAM cells
idea: Mitochondria pack membrane area into folded cristae joined to the body by narrow junctions. In a horizontal 3D DRAM tier, build the lateral capacitor from a thin Si/SiGe sub-superlattice inside the tier. Selectively etch out the SiGe to leave 4-6 thin shelves branching off a narrow neck, then coat them conformally as cristae-like folded electrodes.
why: 3D DRAM capacitor blocker (fact 2): ~3-4x lateral capacitor area per tier footprint, so the stack breaks even with far fewer than 26 tiers. Uses existing epi and selective etch.

title: Tungsten-free BiSb topological spin-Hall write line for nanomagnet bits
idea: Write perpendicular nanomagnets with a BiSb topological-insulator line (spin Hall angle ~10) sputtered at <=250 C after the 350 C MTJ anneal, instead of W/Ta/Pt. The large spin Hall angle cuts the required current density ~10x.
why: ~10x lower SOT write energy and no tungsten (China ~80% chokepoint), in a fully BEOL-stackable magnetic bit.

title: Negative-capacitance boosted cell lets array voltage fall to 0.3 V
idea: Effect walk: ferroelectric negative capacitance. A thin, domain-stabilized ferroelectric layer in series with the storage dielectric raises the stack's effective capacitance ~3x inside the non-hysteretic NC window, so the cell stores the same signal charge at an array voltage of ~0.33 V and wordline ~1.2 V.
why: Breaks the voltage floor (fact 10): bitline CV2 scales with V2, so 1 V to 0.33 V cuts array energy per access ~9-10x while also easing the capacitor wall (fact 1); hysteresis-free NC at GHz rates is disputed.

title: Eliminate junction leakage: nano-electromechanical relay seals each storage node
idea: Eliminate the semiconductor access junction: each capacitor connects to the bitline through a 20-nm electrostatic nano-relay (vertical cantilever across a vacuum gap) that touches only during access; when open, the leakage path is a physical gap, so node leakage drops from ~13 fA to effectively zero. Relays switch in ~1-5 ns at this size, with Ru or carbon contacts for high cycle counts.
why: Kills fact 3 (refresh = 16-33% idle power, 10-20% bandwidth) and lets Cs shrink 3-5x because only sensing, not retention, sets Cs, cutting the AR-75 pillar (fact 1); contact endurance toward 1e15 cycles is the risk.

title: Adobe brick builder: GaN polarization 2DEG node, implant-isolated, no etch
idea: An adobe builder makes walls from sun-dried earth with almost no water. Store charge in an AlGaN/GaN polarization-induced 2DEG pocket under a floating gate, and isolate neighbouring cells with a nitrogen implant that kills the 2DEG instead of etching mesas. The planar epi stack then needs no etch, clean or CMP.
why: A wide-gap storage node with built-in polarization charge (facts 1, 3), on US-manufacturable GaN-on-Si. Defining cells by implant alone cuts water by more than 10x.

title: Macrame hopfions: knotted spin textures stacked as beads in one pillar
idea: Borrow knot-tying. Current pulses write 3D knotted magnetic solitons (hopfions) into a thick Co/Pt/Ir multilayer pillar, several stacked vertically like knots on a cord. Each level's presence or absence is a bit, read by depth-resolved magnetoresistance from a segmented pillar.
why: Fact 2: multi-bit 3D storage in one etched pillar with no transistor tiers. Topological protection gives unlimited endurance at ~4 bits per 4F2 footprint.

title: Po: memory grown by bacteria — magnetosome dipole-chain shift registers
idea: Po: memory is grown by bacteria. Extracted: culture magnetotactic bacteria for uniform 40 nm magnetite crystals, deposit them field-aligned in imprinted grooves, and let dipolar coupling plus a global rotating clock field shift bits along each chain (nanomagnet-logic style), with a few MTJ heads per chain.
why: Biomanufactured magnets at cents per gram, coarse grooves and non-volatile chains aim 100x+ lower $/GB. Trade-offs: us serial access and clock-field power.

title: Zipper: sliding bilayer registry flips polarization by one atom-step
idea: Stimulus 'zipper' (two rows of teeth interlock in one of two registries) -> bilayer hBN or MoS2 stacked AB or BA; a vertical field slides one layer by one bond length, flipping the interfacial polarization, read by tunnel current through the bilayer. Switching is a shear slide, not ion or defect motion, so fatigue is minimal.
why: Sub-nm nonvolatile storage element switching below 0.5 V breaks the CV^2 voltage floor (fact 10) and removes refresh (fact 3); transferable sheets stack as BEOL tiers (fact 2).

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay access device with air-gap zero leakage
idea: Box = {medium: charge on a MIM capacitor | access: 4-terminal NEMS relay with a 5 nm air gap | sense: charge-share SA | integration: relay array in BEOL over the capacitors | substrate: Si | fab: sacrificial release + Pt-coated contacts}. When the relay is open, the only leakage path is the capacitor dielectric, so retention moves from 64 ms to hours and the capacitor can shrink to ~1 fF.
why: Fact 3 leakage tail and Fact 1: removes subthreshold and GIDL tails, eliminates refresh power and bandwidth (16-33% of idle power), and allows 5x smaller capacitors.

title: Hidden charge-density-wave state in 1T-TaS2 as resistive bit
idea: Box = {medium: metastable hidden CDW domain state in 1T-TaS2 | access: Si FET | sense: ~10x resistance ratio | integration: BEOL film | substrate: Si | fab: MBE or CVD TaS2 + hBN encapsulation}. A ps-to-ns current pulse quenches the electron lattice into the hidden metallic CDW state, and a longer, weaker pulse restores the insulating commensurate state; switching is electronic ordering, not atom migration, so energy is fJ-scale.
why: Energy and endurance via purely electronic order switching: fJ writes and no refresh, but the hidden state has only been shown stable at low temperature.

title: Charge-density-wave hidden state as an electrons-only phase bit
idea: Worsen: store bits by moving atoms or ions, which wear out. Flip: store the bit in the electronic order of a charge-density-wave material (1T-TaS2) whose metastable 'hidden' metallic state is set by a ps current pulse and erased by a longer pulse; only electrons reorder, so there is no atomic wear, and resistance contrast is 10-100x.
why: Endurance and speed (ps writes, fJ energy) with non-volatility; attacks refresh and the voltage floor (facts 3, 10). Room-temperature stability is the open question.

title: Splat-quenched charge-density-wave bit in 1T-TaS2 nanoflakes
idea: Use the splat quenching that makes metallic glass. A 30 ps current pulse melts the charge-density-wave order of a 1T-TaS2 flake and refreezes it into a metastable 'hidden' metallic state, and a longer gentle pulse restores the insulating state. The bit is the electronic phase, read as a 10-100x resistance ratio.
why: A purely electronic phase change: no atoms move, so endurance is unlimited (unlike PCM), and switching is ps at fJ energy. The risk is keeping the state stable near room temperature through strain and thickness.

title: Hitachi single-electron polysilicon memory revived on 130-nm lines
idea: Hitachi's 1990s Yano memory stored a few electrons in a polysilicon nanograin that gated a percolation channel. Reproduce it with 3-nm poly-Si or Si-nanocrystal films on existing 130/90-nm lines, where ~10 stored electrons shift the channel threshold enough to read in a 1T gain structure.
why: Few-electron storage removes the capacitor wall (Fact 1) and the Coulomb-blockade barrier extends retention to seconds or more (Fact 3); the storage grain self-assembles, so old-node litho suffices.

title: Ball-and-chain nanomechanical plug isolating each storage node
idea: Voltage-gated K+ channels inactivate when a tethered 'ball' plugs the pore. Give each storage node a vertical nanocantilever contact that touches the bitline only while its wordline electrode pulls it in. When released, a vacuum gap gives essentially zero off-current, so leakage is set only by the capacitor dielectric.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): off-current near zero lets refresh stretch from 64 ms toward minutes. Contact wear must reach >10^15 cycles, using hard Ru or carbon contacts.

title: Self-rolling nanomembrane Swiss-roll capacitors on polymer foil
idea: Invert 'a 3D capacitor must be etched deep into a substrate' -> deposit it flat and let strain roll it up. A strained bilayer (SiNx stress layer plus TiN/HfZrO/TiN stack) patterned on a sacrificial polymer releases and curls into a 5-10 turn micro-tube, multiplying electrode area 10-20x per footprint; whole arrays roll in parallel on polyimide or glass.
why: Reaches fact-1 capacitance from planar deposition plus one release step (EUV-free, low capex) on any substrate; roll diameters below ~200 nm are hard, so it suits a cheap capacity tier.

title: Heat-assisted magnetic recording logic: heat-gated thermionic write barrier
idea: As HAMR writes high-coercivity media only while a laser heats the spot, isolate the storage node behind a ~1.0 eV conduction-band-offset barrier (Si node under an AlN or Ga2O3 spacer) that is opaque at 300 K, and write with a 2-ns pulse in an integrated TaN microheater that lifts the barrier region to ~600 K, where thermionic emission rises ~1e8x.
why: Fact 3: hold-state leakage over a 1 eV barrier is ~1e8 below the write-state current, enabling refresh-free retention; 50-nm heaters have ~1-5 ns thermal time constants, but heater energy (~10-100 fJ) must be shared row-wide to beat refresh savings.
